subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin/API config-write veto hook, and what plugin trust, redaction, ordering, timeout, recursion, and failure semantics should it use across config.set, config.patch, config.apply, and shared config mutation helpers?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing seam, but a hook that can inspect pending config and block persistence changes the plugin trust and security boundary in a way automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design guarded config-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow, documented pre-persistence hook covering RPC and shared mutation paths with explicit redaction, timeout, recursion, and rejection semantics.

options.title: Keep core-only validation
options.body: Keep built-in validation, SecretRef preflight, and agent-write allowlists as the only mandatory controls, while documenting external validators as optional helpers.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight RFC
options.body: Defer this hook until the broader config validation/preflight direction chooses one shared validation contract.

recommendation.title: Design guarded config-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow, documented pre-persistence hook covering RPC and shared mutation paths with explicit redaction, timeout, recursion, and rejection semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed this issue as unresolved config validation/mutation product boundary work and are connected to adjacent config/security history.
